provenance.instrument: East Goshen Township Code Chapter 240 Zoning (Zoning Ordinance of 1997, Ord. No. 119, 6-9-1997, as amended), as published on eCode360
provenance.status_detail: eCode360 code date 2025-07-15 (breadcrumb). New Laws on 2026-11-14: Ord. No. 129-A-2026 (2026-02-17), sewer rentals and charges (Chapter 188), not zoning.
provenance.code_current_through_note: eCode360 breadcrumb 'Code 2025-07-15'. The only New Law (Ord. No. 129-A-2026, sewer rentals) is not zoning.
checks: 'Apartment for care of a relative' is a permitted accessory use in R-2, R-3, R-4 and R-5 (240-9E(16), 240-10E(18), 240-11E(17), 240-12E(16)) and in R-1, which allows the accessory uses permitted in R-2 (240-8D(1)(d)). Accessory uses in 240-32 are 'permitted by right, unless otherwise stated'

The apartment is 'A housing unit especially created for and limited to occupancy by a relative of the residents of the principal dwelling unit, to provide needed care and supervision to such relative' and may also house the relative's spouse (240-6). At most two persons, and at least one needs care and supervision because of old age, disability, handicap, developmental disability or illness (240-32C(2), (3))

Relatives: brother, sister, parent, child, grandparent, great-grandparent, grandchild, great-grandchild, uncle, aunt, niece, nephew, sister-in-law, brother-in-law or parent-in-law, by blood, marriage, adoption or formal foster relationship (240-6)

The unit must be designed so it can easily be reconverted into part of the principal dwelling unit. When the relative no longer lives there it is reconverted or completely removed, kitchen and its plumbing and wiring included, with no exterior evidence left. Before use the owner records an agreement that bars renting it to a nonrelative. The house occupants report changes in adult residents (240-32C(4) to (6))

The apartment may have its own kitchen and may not harm the single-family exterior appearance of the dwelling (240-32C(7), (8)). Otherwise a dwelling unit may not include a second kitchen or a walled-off living area 'unless specifically permitted by this chapter' (240-6 dwelling unit)
No size cap and no parking rule of its own. A dwelling unit with three bedrooms or fewer needs 2 spaces, four or more 3 spaces (240-33)

Historic resources: a Class I or Class II historic resource on the Historic Resources Inventory may be converted into one or more dwelling units by conditional use of the Board of Supervisors, as its one adaptive reuse, with each unit having its own bathroom and kitchen, within the historic resource (240-38.5A(2)(c), B). Except where the district provides otherwise, where several units result from the conversion each has at least 800 sq ft of habitable floor area (240-38.5A(2)(c)[1]). The Board must find the reuse necessary to preserve the resource for reasons other than purely economic grounds (240-38.7). The Board may modify area and bulk rules except height (240-38.6)

Outside R-1 to R-5 the apartment for care of a relative is not listed. 240-4D (conditional use for a similar unlisted use) reaches only a use 'not listed as permitted in any zoning district', and the apartment is listed in R-1 to R-5, so elsewhere the path is a use variance. Only one principal use per lot unless specifically permitted (240-23A)

R-1 planned residential development (PRD): within a PRD, 240-8E(4)(k) applies 'in place of any other setback or height requirements': no building within 15 ft of a paved cartway or of another building, residential buildings 50 ft from the tract's exterior lines and perimeter streets, height at most 30 ft, and the Board of Supervisors may vary these. A PRD lot has no lot minimum of its own (density at least 12,000 sq ft per detached unit on any one acre, 240-8E(1)(c)). The R-2 lot size and yards apply only to a single-family detached dwelling outside a PRD (240-8D(1)(b))
A garage or other structure of 80 sq ft or more accessory to a dwelling may not stand in the required front yard (240-32F). A garage is 'used only for storage purposes' (240-6)
A guest house (240-6) is a separate building for the temporary accommodation of guests in a PRD. It is a commercial use under 240-8D(1)(a)[2], not an ADU
provenance.notes: Zoning office: East Goshen Township Zoning Officer. eCode360 code EA1698 is East Goshen Township, Chester County (Township of East Goshen, PA; Chester County Recorder of Deeds in 240-8). Read on eCode360 in a browser, one page at a time, on 2026-11-14. Code search (all content, New Laws included) for 'accessory apartment', 'accessory dwelling', 'living quarters', 'immediate family', 'in-law', ECHO, 'elder cottage', granny, 'family dwelling', relative, 'housekeeping unit', 'two-family', duplex, caretaker, 'tenant house', 'guest house' and 'accessory living' found the apartment for care of a relative (240-6, 240-32C and the R-2 to R-5 accessory use lists), the PRD guest house definition, and group homes. A second search for unlisted uses, accessory building, 'second dwelling', 'additional dwelling' and 'in-law' found 240-4. Read in full: 240-8 to 240-12, 240-32, 240-23, 240-2, 240-38.5, 240-38.6, the definitions from A to I and RELATED OR RELATIVE. Read on screen: 240-4, 240-33A(1), the residential rows of the 240-33 parking table. 240-38.7 seen only as a search excerpt ('for reasons other than purely economic grounds'). Not read: commercial, industrial and business park use lists (240-14 to 240-21), 240-28 cluster, 240-29 apartments, 240-30 townhouses, 240-36 open space development, 240-31 conditional use standards, 240-38.7 in full, Article VII nonconforming lots, the other definitions after I.

term.value: apartment for care of a relative
term.note: 'A housing unit especially created for and limited to occupancy by a relative of the residents of the principal dwelling unit, to provide needed care and supervision to such relative. Such unit may also house a spouse of such relative.'

status.note: By right as an accessory use, but only for a relative of a permanent resident of the house who needs care and supervision. At most two persons.

status_outside.note: The commercial, industrial and business park use lists were not read. A use not permitted in a district is prohibited there (240-4C). The 240-4D conditional use reaches only a use not listed as permitted in any district, and the apartment for care of a relative is listed in R-1 to R-5, so outside them the path is a use variance.

path.note: 'The following accessory uses, buildings or structures shall be permitted by right, unless otherwise stated'. A use and occupancy permit is issued after the agreement is recorded (240-32C(4)).

fallback_path.note: Relief from a district rule is a variance from the Zoning Hearing Board.

value.name: Residential conversion of a historic resource into dwelling units
value.conditions: Only a structure on the Historic Resources Inventory (Class I or Class II), as one adaptive reuse approved by the Board of Supervisors under 240-31 and 240-38.7. Each unit has its own bathroom and kitchen. Except where the district provides otherwise, where several units result each has at least 800 sq ft of habitable floor area and additions may not raise the unit count. The use is contained within the historic resource. The Board must find the reuse necessary to preserve the resource for reasons other than purely economic grounds (240-38.7). The Board may modify area and bulk rules, never height. Further development of the property, or a subdivision keeping the resource on its own lot, is also a conditional use (240-38.5C, D).

requires.condition: The structure is a Class I or Class II historic resource on the East Goshen Township Historic Resources Inventory

value.note: No relative or care rule. Could turn a historic house or barn into a second unit. 240-38.7 was seen only as a search excerpt.

zoning_districts.note: R-1 by reference to the R-2 accessory uses.

building_types.note: Not limited. Accessory to the 'principal dwelling unit'. The text does not limit the house type. R-3 to R-5 permit semidetached dwellings and R-5 townhouses and apartments.

historic_bypass.note: No historic path for the relative apartment. A historic resource may be converted into dwelling units by conditional use (see the other ways to add a unit).

value.condition: Occupied only by a relative (240-6) of a permanent resident of the house, and may also house the relative's spouse. At most two persons.
At least one resident of the apartment needs care and supervision because of old age, disability, handicap, developmental disability or illness.

Designed and installed so it can easily be reconverted into part of the principal dwelling unit. Reconverted or completely removed when the relative leaves, kitchen and its connections removed, no exterior evidence left. It may not harm the single-family exterior appearance of the dwelling.

Before use the owner records an agreement on a Township form that restricts the apartment and bars renting it to a nonrelative of the current or future owners. The use and occupancy permit follows the recording.

R-4 and R-5: 'All uses in this district shall be serviced by centralized sewage disposal' systems. A lot without public sewer does not meet the district rule. Ask the zoning officer before planning a unit.
R-4 and R-5: all uses are served by a centralized water supply system. A lot without public water does not meet the district rule. Ask the zoning officer before planning a unit.

R-1: if the lot is in a planned residential development (PRD, 240-8D(1)(a)), the R-2 lot size and yards shown do not apply. Within a PRD 240-8E(4)(k) applies 'in place of any other setback or height requirements': no building within 15 ft of a paved cartway or of another building, residential buildings at least 50 ft from the tract's exterior lines and perimeter streets, height at most 30 ft, and the Board of Supervisors may vary these. A PRD lot under one acre is not nonconforming for that reason. Outside a PRD a single-family detached lot follows the R-2 rules: 1 acre (43,560 sq ft), and a smaller lot there may be nonconforming.

types_allowed.note: The unit must be easy to reconvert 'into part of the principal dwelling unit' and may not harm the single-family exterior appearance, read as a unit in or added to the house.

types_in_conflict.note: 240-32C(4) asks for a unit that 'can easily be reconverted into part of the principal dwelling unit', which reads as a unit in or added to the house. The same paragraph lets it 'be completely removed' when the relative leaves, which fits a separate building. The code does not settle a separate new building.

types_not_addressed.note: A garage is 'an accessory building ... which is used only for storage purposes' (240-6). The apartment text does not name a garage.

district_yards_bind_accessory.note: 'Any other size of accessory building shall conform to the applicable yard requirements for principal buildings.' Sheds up to 120 sq ft (240 sq ft on lots over an acre) and 12 ft may stand in the side and rear yards (240-32P(1)).

owner_occupancy.note: No owner occupancy rule. The occupant must be a relative of a permanent resident of the house, and the recorded agreement bars renting to a nonrelative of the owner.

occupancy.value: A relative of a permanent resident of the house, who needs care and supervision, and the relative's spouse. At most two persons. Relative means brother, sister, parent, child, grandparent, great-grandparent, grandchild, great-grandchild, uncle, aunt, niece, nephew, sister-in-law, brother-in-law or parent-in-law, by blood, marriage, adoption or formal foster relationship. Not second cousins or cousins further removed.

max_adus.note: 'A housing unit' for a relative. The code gives no count. Read as one.

reading.value: If the apartment counts as a dwelling unit, it needs 2 more spaces, 4 in total with a house of three bedrooms or fewer. The text leans this way: 240-32C(4) calls it 'Such dwelling unit', an unlisted use takes the most similar listed use (240-33A(1)(b)), and where a use includes more than one type of use the spaces are 'the sum of the parking requirements for each separate use' (240-33A(1)(c)). If it is part of the house's use, the house's 2 (3 with four or more bedrooms) are enough.

setback_front_ft.note: Outside a PRD only, R-2 figures (240-8D(1)(b)). Within a PRD 240-8E(4)(k) applies in place of them. Minimum 45 ft. In subdivisions of two or more lots an average of 60 ft.

setback_side_ft.note: Outside a PRD only, R-2 figures (240-8D(1)(b)). Within a PRD 240-8E(4)(k) applies in place of them. Each of two side yards.

setback_rear_ft.note: Outside a PRD only, R-2 figures (240-8D(1)(b)). Within a PRD 240-8E(4)(k) applies in place of them.

principal_max_height_ft.note: Outside a PRD only, R-2 figures (240-8D(1)(b)). Within a PRD 240-8E(4)(k) applies in place of them. 3 stories and 30 ft.

principal_max_stories.note: Outside a PRD only, R-2 figures (240-8D(1)(b)). Within a PRD 240-8E(4)(k) applies in place of them.

max_building_coverage.note: Outside a PRD only, R-2 figures (240-8D(1)(b)). Within a PRD 240-8E(4)(k) applies in place of them. Lot coverage by buildings 25%: the ground floor area of all principal and accessory buildings (240-6). Total impervious cover 35%.

min_lot_sqft.note: 'All Other Uses' column: 1 acre, width 150 ft at the setback line and 60 ft at the street.

setback_front_ft.note: Minimum 45 ft. In subdivisions of two or more lots an average of 60 ft.

max_building_coverage.note: Lot coverage by buildings 25%: the ground floor area of all principal and accessory buildings (240-6). Total impervious cover 35%.

min_lot_sqft.note: Single-family detached dwelling: 18,000 sq ft, width 100 ft at the setback line and 50 ft at the street. Semidetached 12,000 sq ft with a 20 ft side yard on one side.

setback_front_ft.note: Minimum 30 ft. In subdivisions of two or more lots an average of 40 ft.

max_building_coverage.note: Lot coverage by buildings 25%: the ground floor area of all principal and accessory buildings (240-6). Total impervious cover 35%.

min_lot_sqft.note: Single-family detached dwelling: 14,500 sq ft, width 90 ft at the setback line and 70 ft at the street. Semidetached 10,000 sq ft with a 10 ft side yard on one side. 'All uses in this district shall be serviced by centralized sewage disposal and centralized water supply systems.'

setback_front_ft.note: Minimum 20 ft. In subdivisions of two or more lots an average of 30 ft.

max_building_coverage.note: Lot coverage by buildings 25%: the ground floor area of all principal and accessory buildings (240-6). Total impervious cover 35%.

min_lot_sqft.note: Single-family detached dwelling: 14,000 sq ft, width 85 ft at the setback line and 65 ft at the street. Semidetached 10,000 sq ft with a 10 ft side yard on one side. All uses served by centralized sewage disposal and water supply.
